title: Guangzhou International Finance Center
visualBrief: Guangzhou’s curved triangular blue-glass West Tower, gently swelling shaft, subtle diagrid and three dark mechanical bands, triangular roof skylight and west-offset raised circular helipad.

nativeAxes.front: Reconstructed north frontage; actual doorway bearing not surveyed
nativeAxes.origin: Mapped tower footprint frame at reconstructed street grade

reconstruction.plan: The exact-QID mapped rounded triangle preserves its signed footprint. A smooth interpolated trace removes long flat map segments while retaining the three unequal rounded corners. A continuous large-radius section widens near the lower third and tapers to the roof, following the architect’s elevation.
reconstruction.facade: Physical pane borders and repeated dark mechanical courses follow the curved glass. The engineer’s 27m diagrid stage and 1.8m-to0.95m tube width control the subtle diagonal traces. The built tubes are behind the glazing: tinted conformal strips reproduce their visible daylight appearance over opaque blue glass rather than rendering an exposed white exoskeleton.
reconstruction.roof: The architect plan/section establishes the triangular glazed roof and raised circular helipad at one edge. CVU supplies the437.5m landing plane and438.6m architectural top. Fine rooftop supports, netting and stairs are photographed reconstructions.
reconstruction.ground: A narrow glazed entry and flat canopy reconstruct the tower frontage. The separately mapped mall and apartment annex remain separate map context, preserving this asset’s tower identity.

scaleBasis: Published owner/architect/contractor heights and distinguishing construction systems; map footprint for local orientation, with reconstructed details declared separately.
geometrySource: Original deterministic exterior geometry; no downloaded meshes or copied photographic textures. Footprint-derived registration includes separately attributed OpenStreetMap evidence.
sourceLicense: Original reconstruction under repository license. Map-derived plan evidence: © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0. Reference publications are linked, not redistributed.
materialMethod: Canonical shared material graphs bound through molenSurface extras with metric coordinates divided by central repeat meters. Vertex colors provide component tint. Glass retains opaque metallic-roughness PBR; no bitmap texture copies per model.
reviewStatus: source-geometry; near/far and shared-material captures pending
limitations: Original 36534-triangle, 3902148-byte source master remains exactly reproducible from unchanged recipe. Reviewed source corrects the buried inward-facing entrance with outward panels conforming to the curved facade, 14 cm beyond its elevation-dependent trace, and preserves the rounded triangular shaft, restrained visible diagrid behind opaque tinted glazing, three mechanical bands, triangular skylight/roof, west-offset raised circular helipad, H marking, supports/net/stairs, IFC strokes and north canopy. Fine curtain-wall seals were already omitted from this source recipe and are not claimed. Separate mall, apartments, interiors and site landscaping are excluded. Skyline averages the subtle diagrid and omits letters/rails/net/separate door frames; district restores coarse tinted diagonal traces; street restores split diagonal traces and aggregate net/stairs/letter sampling; close-up preserves original detailed components. Shared painted-metal graph approximates coated trim/supports; opaque blue glazing uses vertex tint, with two draw groups and zero embedded images. Site envelope is mapped, while swelling, helipad exact position, entrance, fine bands and equipment are reconstructions. Finite along-ray 1.5/.75/.3/.1 m allowances are for sampled main surfaces, excluding omitted decorative strips/net/letters/rails; no global error or surveyed grade/device performance claim.
importReason: Preserve thin facade frames, panel joints and crown/antenna details until a measured LOD chain is authored.
